x: State Legislatures are in Part VI, Articles 168–212. Parliament is in Part V, Articles 79–122.
t: Discriminate Part V (Parliament) from Part VI (State Legislatures).

x: Under Article 168, a State Legislature is the Governor plus the Assembly, and in bicameral States also the Legislative Council.
t: Remember that the Governor is part of every State Legislature.

x: Assembly elections are direct, use first-past-the-post, are run by the Election Commission of India, and rest on adult suffrage (Article 326). The answer is a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i.
t: Recall who conducts Assembly elections and on what basis.

x: Both are true: Article 164(2) makes the State Council of Ministers collectively answerable to the Legislative Assembly. R gives the provision behind A.
t: Recall Article 164(2).

x: Option B is incorrect: an Assembly member must be at least 25; 30 is the age for the Council. An Assembly has 60 to 500 members (Article 170) and is the lower, popular House.
t: Discriminate the Assembly's minimum age (25) from the Council's (30).

x: Uttar Pradesh has the largest Legislative Assembly, with 403 members.
t: Recall the 403 seats of Uttar Pradesh.

x: Both are true: Sikkim has the smallest State Assembly (32 members), and Puducherry the smallest Union Territory Assembly (33: 30 elected, 3 nominated).
t: Discriminate the smallest State Assembly (Sikkim) from the smallest UT Assembly (Puducherry).
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Sikkim has the smallest State Legislative Assembly, with 32 members.
Statement B: Puducherry has the smallest Union Territory Assembly, with 33 members.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

x: All three are correct: Article 332 reserves seats for SCs and STs by population, the 104th Amendment ended Anglo-Indian nomination (Article 333), and the 106th (2023) reserves about one-third of seats for women after the next delimitation.
t: Recall the 104th and 106th Amendments.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Article 332 provides for reservation of seats for SCs and STs based on population ratios.
II. The 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2020 ended the nomination of Anglo-Indian members under Article 333.
III. The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023 provides approximately one-third reservation for women in directly elected Assembly seats, effective after post-census delimitation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Option B is incorrect: the Legislative Council is the permanent House, with one-third retiring every two years. The Assembly has a five-year term and can be dissolved.
t: Discriminate the dissolvable Assembly from the permanent Council.

x: A State Money Bill can be introduced only in the Legislative Assembly, which has the final say. The Council can only recommend within 14 days.
t: Recall the Assembly's power over Money Bills.

x: I and II are correct: the Council can delay an ordinary bill for at most four months, three the first time and one the second. III is false because it cannot block the bill.
t: Recall the Council's 3 + 1 month limit.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. A Legislative Council can delay an ordinary Bill for a maximum of four months.
II. The first delay may be three months and the second delay one month.
III. The Legislative Council can permanently block an ordinary Bill.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: A is true: the Speaker stays in office after dissolution until the new Assembly first meets. B is false because the Speaker has only a casting vote when votes are tied, not a first vote.
t: Discriminate a first-instance vote from a casting vote.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Speaker continues in office after dissolution of the Assembly until immediately before the first meeting of the newly elected Assembly.
Statement B: The Speaker votes in the first instance and also has a casting vote in case of a tie.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

x: The Governor decides ordinary disqualifications (Articles 191/192) on the Election Commission's binding opinion. The Speaker decides defection cases, subject to judicial review. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv.
t: Discriminate Article 191 disqualification (Governor) from Tenth Schedule defection (Speaker).

x: Option C is incorrect: under Article 176, the Governor addresses the legislature at the first session after each general election and at the first session of each year.
t: Recall the two occasions for the Governor's address.

x: Both are true: a State ordinance lapses six weeks after the legislature reassembles, and the Governor issues ordinances only during a recess. Issuing it in recess does not explain the six-week limit, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether the timing of issue explains the lapse period.

x: All three are correct: a State ministry may be at most 15% of the Assembly and at least 12 Ministers, and a non-member can be a Minister for at most six months.
t: Recall the ministry limits and the six-month rule.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The State Council of Ministers may have a maximum strength of 15% of the Assembly strength.
II. The minimum number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, is 12.
III. A non-member minister may hold office for a maximum of six consecutive months without being elected.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Article 170 covers Assembly composition, 173 the age qualification, 178 the Speaker and Deputy Speaker, and 213 ordinances. The answer is a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall Articles 170, 173, 178 and 213.

x: Tamil Nadu has no Legislative Council. The six bicameral States are Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
t: Recall the six States with Legislative Councils.

x: All four are correct: Article 169 covers creating or abolishing a Council, 198–199 State Money Bills, 200–201 assent and reservation, and 192 the Governor's decision on disqualification.
t: Recall Articles 169, 192, 198 to 201.

x: The Election Commission of India conducts Assembly elections under Article 324. State Election Commissions conduct only Panchayat and municipal elections.
t: Discriminate the Election Commission of India from State Election Commissions.

x: Option A is incorrect: the Speaker does not vote in the first instance, but has a casting vote when votes are tied. The Assembly elects the Speaker from its members.
t: Discriminate a first-instance vote from a casting vote.

x: Option C is incorrect: the Governor does not address every session, only the first after a general election and the first of each year (Article 176).
t: Recall the two occasions for the Governor's address.

x: Both are true and R explains A: Article 172(1) is the provision that lets Parliament extend an Assembly's term during an Emergency, one year at a time and not beyond six months after it ends.
t: Check whether R states the constitutional source of the power in A.
s:
Assertion (A): Parliament may extend the term of a State Legislative Assembly during a National Emergency.
Reason (R): Article 172(1) permits Parliament to extend the Assembly's term by law while a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

x: A is true: the Assembly is directly elected. B is false because the Council is indirectly elected by single transferable vote, with some members nominated.
t: Discriminate the directly elected Assembly from the indirectly elected Council.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The State Legislative Assembly is directly elected by citizens.
Statement B: The Legislative Council is elected only through direct election by citizens.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

x: A is true: the Chairman presides over the Legislative Council (Article 182). B is false because the Speaker presides over the Assembly.
t: Match each House to its presiding officer.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Chairman is the presiding officer of the Legislative Council.
Statement B: The Speaker is the presiding officer of the Legislative Council.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

x: All four are correct: under Articles 200–201, the Governor can assent, withhold assent, return an ordinary bill, or reserve a bill for the President.
t: Recall the Governor's four options on a bill.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Governor may give assent to a State Bill.
II. The Governor may withhold assent to a State Bill.
III. The Governor may return an ordinary Bill for reconsideration.
IV. The Governor may reserve a Bill for the President's consideration.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Article 176 covers the Governor's address, 197 the Council's delay of ordinary bills, 207 the Governor's recommendation for Money Bills, and 201 bills reserved for the President. The answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
t: Recall Articles 176, 197, 201 and 207.

x: The Speaker resigns to the Deputy Speaker and the Deputy Speaker to the Speaker. The Assembly elects the Speaker, who has a casting vote on a tie. The answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Remember that the two presiding officers resign to each other.

x: Both are true: most Council members are indirectly elected by single transferable vote, and one-sixth are nominated by the Governor.
t: Recall how the Council is chosen.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Members of a Legislative Council are chosen through indirect election by the proportional representation system using the single transferable vote.
Statement B: A Legislative Council may also contain nominated members.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

x: I, II and III are correct: the Council is permanent, one-third retire every two years, and members serve six years. IV is false because it is never dissolved.
t: Find the statement that dissolves the permanent Council.
s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Legislative Council:
I. It is a permanent body.
II. One-third of its members retire every two years.
III. Each member has a six-year term.
IV. It is subject to dissolution after every five years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: The Assembly is the lower, popular House with a minimum age of 25, and the Council the upper House (House of Elders) with a minimum age of 30. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Pair each House with its nickname and minimum age.

x: Both are true: under Article 174, the Governor summons, prorogues and dissolves the Assembly, and no more than six months may pass between sessions.
t: Recall Article 174.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Governor summons, prorogues and dissolves the State Legislative Assembly.
Statement B: The maximum permissible gap between two sessions of the State Legislature is six months.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

x: Option A is incorrect: the Governor may return an ordinary bill, but the Constitution sets no time limit for acting on it. The Governor can also assent or withhold assent.
t: Recall that no time limit is fixed for the Governor.

x: Under Article 200, the Governor assents to, withholds assent from, returns, or reserves a State bill. Article 213 is ordinances and 174 sessions.
t: Recall Article 200.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the Assembly's special-majority resolution is only the precondition. Parliament acts by simple majority because Article 169(3) says such a law is not an amendment under Article 368.
t: Ask why a simple majority suffices, not what must happen first.

x: I, II and III are correct: the 91st Amendment (2003) caps a State ministry at 15% of the Assembly, with a minimum of 12. IV is false because the minimum is 12, not six.
t: Recall the minimum of 12.
s:
Consider the following statements regarding the State Council of Ministers:
I. Its maximum strength is capped at 15% of the Assembly strength.
II. Its minimum strength is 12 ministers, including the Chief Minister.
III. The maximum-strength cap was introduced by the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003.
IV. Its minimum strength is six ministers, including the Chief Minister.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Three are correct: the Speaker's Money Bill certificate is final, the Governor must recommend the bill, and the Council has 14 days. Statement 4 is false because the Council cannot block a Money Bill.
t: Find the statement that gives the Council a veto.

x: Both are true: only a Legislative Council can be created or abolished, never the Assembly, and defection cases in the Council are decided by its Chairman under the Tenth Schedule.
t: Remember the presiding officer of each House decides its defection cases.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Legislative Assembly cannot be abolished.
Statement B: Under the Tenth Schedule, the Chairman decides defection cases arising in the Legislative Council.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true

x: Both are true: under Article 168, a unicameral legislature is the Governor and Assembly, and a bicameral one adds the Legislative Council.
t: Remember that the Governor is part of every State Legislature.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: In a unicameral State, the State Legislature consists of the Governor and the Legislative Assembly.
Statement B: In a bicameral State, the State Legislature consists of the Governor, Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

x: Both are true: Assembly elections use first-past-the-post, so the candidate with the most votes wins even without 50%. R explains A.
t: Ask whether first-past-the-post explains winning without a majority.

x: Under Article 178, the Assembly elects both its Speaker and Deputy Speaker from among its own members.
t: Recall Article 178.

x: The Assembly rests on Article 170 and the Council on Article 171. The minimum ages are 25 and 30. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Discriminate Article 170 (Assembly) from 171 (Council).

x: Option C is incorrect: Sikkim's Assembly, the smallest, has 32 seats. Goa and Mizoram have 40 each. Uttar Pradesh has 403, and the general limits are 60 to 500.
t: Recall the smallest Assemblies: Sikkim 32, Goa and Mizoram 40.

x: Three are correct: the Assembly serves five years, one-third of the Council retires every two years, and Council members serve six years. Statement 4 is false because the Council is permanent.
t: Find the statement that makes the Council temporary.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Article 198 itself bars a Money Bill from the Council, and the Council's 14-day recommendatory role is a separate limit that follows, not the reason for the rule.
t: Separate where a Money Bill may originate from what the Council may do with it.

x: The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly alone certifies whether a bill is a Money Bill, and the decision is final.
t: Recall who certifies Money Bills.

x: State Money Bills are under Articles 198–199, the Governor's recommendation under 207, and the Council's delays are three months, then one month. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.
t: Recall Articles 198, 199 and 207 and the 3 + 1 month delays.

x: I, II and IV are correct: the Assembly's term is five years, it can be extended a year at a time in an Emergency, and not beyond six months after the Emergency ends. III is false because the extension is limited.
t: Recall the six-month limit after an Emergency.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The normal term of a State Legislative Assembly is five years.
II. During a National Emergency, Parliament may extend the Assembly’s duration by law for one year at a time.
III. Such extension may continue without limit after the National Emergency ceases.
IV. The extension cannot continue beyond six months after the Emergency ceases.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Option C is incorrect: under Article 192, the Governor decides disqualification questions on the Election Commission's opinion. Insolvency, unsound mind and office of profit are grounds.
t: Recall who decides Article 191 disqualifications.

x: Both are true: under Article 192, the Governor must get the Election Commission's opinion and act on it, so they cannot decide alone. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the binding opinion explains why the Governor cannot act alone.

x: A is true: the resolution needs a special majority (50% of total membership and two-thirds present and voting). B is false because it does not oblige the Union to bring a bill.
t: Discriminate a recommendation from a binding direction.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: An Assembly resolution for creation or abolition of a Legislative Council requires a Special Majority.
Statement B: Once such a resolution is passed, the Union Government is compelled to introduce a Bill in Parliament.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

x: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Bihar and Maharashtra all have Legislative Councils. Goa, Mizoram, Sikkim and Puducherry do not.
t: Recall the six States with Legislative Councils.

x: The Assembly can be dissolved and has a five-year term, the Council is permanent, Money Bills start only in the Assembly, and the Council's second delay is one month. The answer is a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.
t: Pair each House with its features.

x: I, II and III are correct: Article 332 reserves Assembly seats for SCs and STs in proportion to their population. IV is false because States such as Mizoram and Nagaland have no SC-reserved seats.
t: Watch for "every State": reservation depends on each group's population there.
s:
Consider the following statements regarding reservation in State Legislative Assemblies:
I. Seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in State Legislative Assemblies.
II. Reservation is in proportion to the population of the concerned group in the State.
III. The reservation is provided under Article 332.
IV. Seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes in every State Assembly, including Mizoram and Nagaland.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: All four are correct: Sikkim's Assembly is the smallest State Assembly at 32 seats, and Puducherry's the smallest UT Assembly at 33 (30 elected, 3 nominated).
t: Discriminate the smallest State Assembly from the smallest UT Assembly.

x: The Assembly rests on Article 170 and the Council on 171. A Council member must be 30, and a Council must have at least 40 members. The answer is a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i.
t: Recall the Council's age of 30 and minimum of 40.

x: Three qualify: Goa and Mizoram have 40 seats each and Sikkim 32. Puducherry has 33 seats but is a Union Territory, not a State.
t: Check both the seat number and whether each is a State.
s:
How many of the following are States whose Legislative Assemblies have 40 seats or fewer?
1. Goa
2. Mizoram
3. Puducherry
4. Sikkim

x: Assembly members are directly elected from single-member territorial constituencies, by first-past-the-post.
t: Recall the Assembly's constituencies.

x: All three are correct: Assembly elections use adult suffrage (Article 326) and are conducted by the Election Commission of India.
t: Recall Articles 324 and 326.
s:
Consider the following statements about elections to the State Legislative Assembly:
I. Elections are conducted under universal adult suffrage.
II. The elections are conducted by the Election Commission of India.
III. The constitutional reference for universal adult suffrage is Article 326.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Option D is incorrect: losing citizenship is a ground for disqualification under Article 191, along with office of profit, unsound mind and insolvency.
t: Recall the grounds in Article 191.

x: Both are true: an Article 169 resolution only recommends, which is why it does not force the Union to bring a bill. R explains A.
t: Ask whether a recommendation's nature explains its lack of force.

x: A Legislative Council can have at most one-third of the Assembly's strength (Article 171), with a minimum of 40.
t: Recall the one-third ceiling.

x: On a Money Bill, the Council can only recommend. The Assembly may accept or reject those recommendations, and the bill is then passed.
t: Recall the Council's recommendatory role.

x: Under Article 165(1), the Governor appoints the State's Advocate General. The President appoints the Attorney General of India.
t: Pair the Attorney General (President) with the Advocate General (Governor).

x: Option A is incorrect: the Advocate General has no fixed term and serves at the Governor's pleasure under Article 165(3). They are the State's highest law officer and legal adviser.
t: Recall the Advocate General's tenure.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Article 165(1) is what requires the Advocate General to be qualified as a High Court judge; R only says where those qualifications are listed.
t: Check whether R gives the cause of A or only a cross-reference.

x: The Advocate General is under Article 165 (Part VI) and the Attorney General under Article 76 (Part V). The Solicitor General assists the Attorney General. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-ii.
t: Pair Article 76 (Attorney General) with Article 165 (Advocate General).

x: I, II and III are correct: under Article 177, the Advocate General can speak in both Houses, join joint sittings and sit on committees. IV is false because they cannot vote.
t: Discriminate the right to speak from the right to vote.

x: All three are correct: the Advocate General serves at the Governor's pleasure, not the Cabinet's or the Chief Minister's.
t: Recall whose pleasure the Advocate General serves at.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: R only lists one of the duties found in Article 165(2); describing the content of the duties does not explain why they sit in that clause.
t: Ask whether R gives a cause or merely restates part of A.

x: A State Legislature's two Houses are the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council. The Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha belong to Parliament.
t: Discriminate the State Houses from the Houses of Parliament.

x: Both are true: the Solicitor General's office is statutory, not constitutional, and the Attorney General serves the Union government.
t: Discriminate the constitutional Attorney General from the statutory Solicitor General.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Solicitor General of India has a non-constitutional, statutory basis.
Statement B: The jurisdiction level of the Attorney General of India is the Union Government.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

x: The President appoints the Attorney General and the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet the Solicitor General. The Attorney General needs Supreme Court judge qualifications and the Solicitor General must be a senior advocate. The answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Compare the two law officers' appointment and qualifications.

x: The Attorney General serves at the President's pleasure and can speak in Parliament (Article 88). The Solicitor General has a fixed statutory term and no such rights. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
t: Compare the two law officers' tenure and rights in Parliament.

x: All four are correct: Article 88 gives rights in Parliament and 177 in the State Legislature, and 124(3) sets Supreme Court judges' qualifications and 217 High Court judges'.
t: Pair each Union Article with its State parallel.

x: The President appoints High Court judges. The Governor appoints the Advocate General, and the Appointments Committee the Solicitor General.
t: Discriminate who appoints judges from who appoints law officers.
